content.user_title: Review Code with a Senior Checklist
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security, testing, and maintainability issues. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured review steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides review scope discovery from tickets and pull request descriptions.
Uses a checklist for quality, security, performance, and maintainability.
Recommends project-specific linting, testing, and static analysis commands.
Structures feedback with rationale, severity, and suggested fixes.
Supports follow-up verification after fixes are made.
limitations: Does not execute tools by itself; the active assistant must run commands when available.
Depends on the context and diffs provided by the user or repository.
May miss issues outside the visible change set.
Does not replace project-specific reviewer judgment or domain requirements.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to find correctness, test coverage, security, and maintainability issues before merge.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reviews
use_cases.description: Create consistent review expectations across a team and track follow-up verification after fixes.

use_cases.title: Check Solo Changes
use_cases.description: Check changes for common risks before release when another reviewer is not available.

prompt_templates.title: Basic PR Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for correctness, tests, security, and maintainability. Return only actionable findings with severity and rationale.
prompt_templates.scenario: First review of a small pull request

prompt_templates.title: Checklist-Based Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the review-code checklist to the current diff. Group findings by quality, security, performance, and maintainability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured review using the included checklist

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this release candidate for merge risk. Prioritize blocking issues, missing tests, rollback concerns, and follow-up verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Pre-release review for a risky change

prompt_templates.title: Architecture-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan and execute a senior-level review of this design-heavy change. Evaluate coupling, cohesion, interfaces, error handling, and maintenance risk.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of broad architectural changes

output_examples.input: Review a small bug fix before merge.
output: Summary: The change is focused and likely safe.
Finding: Add a regression test for the reported edge case.
Follow-up: Re-run the relevant unit tests after the fix.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that changes authorization logic.
output: Summary: The change needs careful security review.
Finding: Confirm role checks cover both read and write paths.
Follow-up: Add tests for denied access and admin access.

best_practices: Provide the relevant diff, test results, and product context before requesting review.
Ask for severity labels when many findings are expected.
Run available tests and linters before asking for final approval.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for approval without sharing the changed files or diff.
Do not treat the checklist as a substitute for project requirements.
Do not ignore follow-up verification after fixes are applied.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends useful commands, but the active assistant or user must run available tools.

faq.question: Can it review security changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The checklist includes validation, authorization, secrets, cryptography, error messages, and dependency risks.

faq.question: Does it need a pull request?
faq.answer: No. It can review local diffs, copied code, or a planned change when enough context is provided.

faq.question: Will it produce line-specific findings?
faq.answer: It can when file names and line numbers are available in the workspace or diff.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow gives a clear sequence: understand scope, apply the checklist, document findings, and verify fixes.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
